mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 1.0%) reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% indicates a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE falls below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal robust consumer demand, which accelerates corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the central bank's policy rate hikes compress equity valuations through higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO rises.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% (as measured by GDPC1) signals strong economic expansion, which increases corporate profitability and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a robust labor market that fuels consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), the Federal Reserve is likely to implement aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%.
